healthy.causes: A healthy leaf does not show the selected disease category. This classification does not guarantee that the plant is disease-free.
healthy.prevention: Maintain appropriate watering, good airflow, and regular plant inspection. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
healthy.management: Continue routine plant care and monitor for new spots, yellowing, or other changes.

early_blight.symptoms: Tomato early blight commonly causes brown leaf spots, often with concentric rings and surrounding yellowing.
early_blight.causes: Early blight is commonly associated with the fungus Alternaria solani. Warm, humid conditions and wet foliage can favour disease development.
early_blight.prevention: Use healthy planting material, improve airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and remove infected plant debris appropriately.
early_blight.management: Inspect affected plants, remove infected leaves when appropriate, and avoid overhead watering. Seek local agricultural guidance for suitable disease-control measures.

late_blight.symptoms: Tomato late blight can cause irregular dark or water-soaked lesions on leaves, sometimes with pale growth in humid conditions.
late_blight.causes: Late blight is caused by Phytophthora infestans, a disease-causing organism that can spread rapidly in favourable cool, humid conditions.
late_blight.prevention: Monitor plants regularly, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, improve airflow, and follow local agricultural disease alerts.
late_blight.management: Promptly seek local agricultural advice if late blight is suspected because it can spread rapidly. Follow locally approved management recommendations.
